Gastrointestinal bleeding (*gastrointestinal blødning*) is a clinical condition that serves as a critical component in the monitoring of anticoagulation safety within the Danish healthcare system. Specifically, it is recognized as one of the four distinct types of severe bleeding that constitute the outcome variable for Indicator 7, a national quality indicator tracking bleeding incidents among patients with existing atrial fibrillation [^src1]. 

In the context of the annual "Atrieflimren i Danmark" (Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark) report published by the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut), severe bleeding is strictly defined to include intracranial bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding, urinary tract bleeding, and bleeding from the lungs [^src1]. This standardized definition allows health authorities to accurately assess and compare the safety of anticoagulation treatments across national, regional, and local health cluster levels. The indicator's methodology is linked to internationally recognized criteria from the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) and relies on registry data from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregistret).

Because the available corpus data for this specific entity is limited to its definitional role within Indicator 7, further clinical or epidemiological details regarding gastrointestinal bleeding itself are not documented in this extract.
